story.title: Fraud rule update: velocity check for card-not-present payments
story.description: Update the fraud rule in fraud-engine to add a rolling velocity check for card-not-present payments. The payment-service must supply the existing payment event attributes and apply the returned screening decision before posting. The risk engine provides the current policy signal used when the threshold is exceeded. Block the sixth attempt for the same card token within a rolling sixty-second window, including declined attempts. This change shares the payment screening path and core-payments deployment with ST-101, so both stories must agree on rule ordering, combined regression coverage and rollout timing.
acceptance_criteria: The first five card-not-present attempts for one card token inside sixty seconds are evaluated normally; the sixth is blocked by the velocity rule.
Declined attempts count toward the velocity window, while distinct card tokens maintain independent counters.
fraud-engine includes the active risk-engine policy signal and rule version in its screening decision.
Combined ST-101 and ST-110 regression evidence confirms premium payment limits cannot bypass fraud screening; their core-payments release order is agreed.

requirement.business_summary: Card-not-present payments will be screened by a new rolling velocity rule: the first five attempts on a single card token within sixty seconds are evaluated normally, and the sixth is blocked. Declined attempts count toward the window, while each distinct card token keeps its own counter. The rule supports the existing premium payment limit controls rather than replacing them, so limit checks cannot be bypassed by fraud screening.
requirement.technical_summary: The fraud-engine rule set gains a rolling sixty-second velocity counter keyed by card token for card-not-present payment events, counting declined attempts and blocking the sixth attempt. The screening decision returned by fraud-engine continues to be applied by payment-service before posting, and fraud-engine now includes the active risk-engine policy signal and the rule version in that decision. Rule ordering, combined regression coverage and release ordering are shared with ST-101 on the core-payments deployment.
affected_capabilities: Fraud rule versioning and policy signal exposure
requirement.engineering_scope: Small, contained change: one velocity rule added to the existing fraud rule set in fraud-engine, keyed by card token with a sixty-second rolling window and a sixth-attempt block. No new service, endpoint, schema or auth change; payment-service and risk-engine continue to use their existing screening call and policy signal. Main coordination work is rule ordering, combined ST-101/ST-110 regression evidence and agreed core-payments release timing.

tests.title: Risk Engine active policy signal appears in fraud velocity screening decision
steps: Publish an updated risk policy threshold via PUT /risk/policies/{id} and read the active policy version through GET /risk/policies/{id}.
Submit a card-not-present payment screening request to POST /fraud/screenings for a card token.
Inspect the returned fraud screening decision.
tests.expected: The fraud screening decision includes the active risk-engine policy signal and the fraud rule version, and the velocity rule is evaluated using that policy context.

tests.title: Risk Engine policy version is returned with each fraud velocity check decision
steps: Retrieve the current active risk policy version from GET /risk/policies/{id}.
Call POST /fraud/velocity-checks five times within sixty seconds for the same card token, including at least one declined attempt.
Call POST /fraud/velocity-checks for the sixth attempt on that card token.
tests.expected: The sixth attempt is blocked, and the response includes the same active risk-engine policy version and fraud rule version as read from the policy endpoint.

tests.title: Risk Engine policy signal does not bypass premium payment limits for card-not-present payments
steps: Ensure an active risk policy signal is available from GET /risk/policies/{id}.
Submit a card-not-present payment that exceeds the premium payment daily limit but has fewer than six velocity attempts on its card token.
Observe the fraud screening decision and the transaction ledger posting outcome.
tests.expected: The fraud decision carries the active risk-engine policy signal and rule version, but the payment is still blocked by the existing premium payment limit control and no ledger entry is posted.

tests.summary: Selected 5 catalog tests and 3 new tests, covering 3 of 3 impacted nodes (100%); estimated effort is 5.0 hours.

frameworks.reason: No impacted PII-bearing component and no customer-data touch.
card-data components are impacted; the change touches card data.

findings.text: fraud-engine carries card and financial data classes and the rule set gains a rolling sixty-second counter keyed by card token, so card-token handling, storage minimization and masking expectations within the velocity path warrant verification before release.

The new decision path combines the card-not-present screening outcome with a risk-engine policy signal and a rule version, and the rule is authored through fraud-engine.rule-update; access restrictions, authentication and audit logging on the screening, velocity and rule-update endpoints should be checked for card-data exposure.

Declined attempts count toward the window, meaning declined card-not-present events are retained in the velocity state; the duration and content of that retention should be checked against card data minimization expectations, including what is propagated downstream to transaction-db.

recommendations: Verify card-token handling, masking and minimization for the rolling velocity counter and for the screening decision returned by fraud-engine, including whether declined-attempt data is held beyond the sixty-second window.
Confirm access restrictions, authentication and audit logging on fraud-engine.screen, fraud-engine.velocity and fraud-engine.rule-update before release.
Check that embedding the risk-engine policy signal and rule version in the fraud-engine decision does not broaden card data reachable through the screening path.

frameworks.reason: financial-data components are impacted; the change touches financial data.

findings.text: fraud-engine screening decisions gate whether card-not-present payments proceed to posting in transaction-db, and the sixth-attempt block changes which payments reach the ledger; completeness and accuracy of the resulting financial records should be tested.

The decision now carries a fraud rule version and an active risk-engine policy version, and both are publishable through fraud-engine.rule-update and risk-engine.policy-update; change control and attributable audit records over those versioned control updates require verification.

The change is described as supporting existing premium payment limit controls rather than replacing them; evidence that limit checks remain independently enforced and cannot be bypassed by the new velocity rule should be examined.

recommendations: Reconcile postings in transaction-db against fraud-engine screening outcomes around the change, and confirm blocked sixth attempts and declined-attempt outcomes are recorded completely and immutably.
Verify that fraud-engine.rule-update and risk-engine.policy-update retain versioned, attributable audit records with documented control-owner approval for the new velocity rule.
Test that premium payment limit controls still apply independently of the fraud screening path and document the evidence.

findings.text: fraud-engine is the directly changed component with criticality 9 and tier1 service expectations, owned by Payments Platform; service-owner approval, rollback planning and coordination of the shared core-payments release timing with ST-101 represent review exposure.

The decision now depends on a risk-engine policy signal and feeds postings into transaction-db, so cross-team ownership sign-off for Data & Analytics and Core Banking dependencies should be confirmed before the rule is enabled.
Rule ordering within the existing fraud rule set and the described combined ST-101/ST-110 regression evidence are coordination points that warrant documented verification rather than assumption.

recommendations: Obtain Payments Platform and Core Banking service-owner approvals for the fraud-engine change, and record the rollback plan and agreed core-payments release ordering shared with ST-101.
Verify operational monitoring, alerting and authorization tests for the new velocity rule, together with evidence of the combined ST-101/ST-110 regression run.
Confirm documented ownership sign-off for the risk-engine policy signal dependency and for the downstream transaction-db posting path.

triggered_rules: GO: no blocking or conditional release rules fired
rollback_plan: Start rollback with the core-payments deployment group by reverting fraud-engine and then risk-engine to their last approved versions and disabling any configured feature flags.
Then roll back the core-banking deployment group by reverting transaction-db to its prior approved version, with no schema migration rollback required because changes_db_schema is false.
Finally, confirm monitoring shows payment screening and velocity metrics have returned to baseline and notify core-payments, core-banking owners and stakeholders that rollback is complete.
deployment_notes: Deploy the core-banking deployment group first by applying the transaction-db release with no schema migration because changes_db_schema is false.
Deploy the core-payments deployment group next by releasing risk-engine before fraud-engine, then enabling any configured feature flags and validating combined ST-101/ST-110 regression evidence.
Monitor payment screening, velocity counters and policy signal exposure during rollout, and notify core-banking, core-payments owners and stakeholders after each group completes.
